thread.title: Dow Futures Lag As Apple Rises, But Fed, Earnings Limit Gains

author: EdJenner
title: Dow Futures Lag As Apple Rises, But Fed, Earnings Limit Gains
text:
Go to Article
Apple’s ( AAPL ) fiscal Q2 results were the seismic event holding stock futures to positive premarket trade on Wednesday. But despite the boost, S&P 500 and Dow futures lagged with weak gains, as investors cautiously awaited news from the Federal Reserve, and from a heavyweight list of earnings reports including Mastercard ( MA ) and Tesla ( TSLA ).
X
Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 0.3%, with Apple easily leading the index , while earnings-fueled losses from Gilead Sciences ( GILD ) and Incy ( INCY ) held back the advance. Dow Jones industrials futures edged up 0.2%, while S&P 500 futures rose less than 0.1% above fair value. Apple Nears Alt. Buy Point, Drives European Trade
Apple swung nearly 4% higher on better-than-forecast earnings and revenue, a 16% dividend increase and the launch of a $100 billion share buy back program . Apple shares have been locked in consolidations since late January. The current consolidation is a flat base with a 183.60 buy point, and an alternative entry at 179.04. Apple’s after-hours gain Tuesday implied an open back above the stock’s 50-day moving average and 2% below the base’s alternative entry. Stock moves made in extended or premarket trading do not necessarily carry through into the regular session.
Apple also helped boost Europe’s markets, which traded unevenly higher despite data showing eurozone manufacturing slowed to a 13-month low in April. Germany’s DAX led the advance among Europe’s top benchmarks, up 1.1% near midday. Shares of Switzerland-based AMS, maker of the facial recognition software used in iPhones, surged more than 8%. Fed Rate Watch
Investors largely expect no change in policy from this afternoon’s announcement. The CME Group’s FedWatch Tool shows futures pointing to a 94.3% probability of a vote to hold rate targets at their current 1.5%-1.75% range. But the Fed’s comments will be carefully parsed for any indication of how future hikes may play out, or of any change to the committee’s view on the economy . Crude Oil Prices, Inventories Data
Oil names including Concho Resources ( CXO ) and Viper Energy Partners ( VNOM ) went nowhere in premarket trade, despite reporting first-quarter earnings beats late Tuesday, as crude oil prices dropped nearly 2% for the day. American Petroleum Institute data released Tuesday showed a 3.4 million-barrel increase in oil stockpiles, vs. expectations for an increase of 739,000 barrels. Gasoline inventories rose 1.6 million barrels, confounding forecasts for a 587,000-barrel decrease. The API data is a precursor to the weekly crude stockpiles report from the Energy Information Administration, due for release at 10:30 a.m. ET.
Crude oil prices added 0.1% early Wednesday, with U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate holding just above $67 a barrel. That is a bit more than 3% below the 41-month high set on April 19. Cirrus Leads Chip Stocks, Shutterfly Eyes Buy Point, Snap Dives
Chip stocks were generally positive, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index looking to add a third straight gain. The index surged 1.7% on Tuesday. Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) and Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ) led in premraket trade, up nearly 3% apiece. Cirrus reports its fiscal fourth-quarter results after today’s closing bell. Skyworks reports late Thursday.
Milpitas, Calif.-based chipmaker Nanometrics ( NANO ) spiked 10% after scoring a huge first-quarter sales and profit beat late Tuesday.
Juniper Networks ( JNPR ) surged 8% after reporting its first-quarter results late Tuesday. Terex ( TEX ) and Ocwen Financial ( OCN ) each muscled up more than 6% following their early Wednesday reports.
Shutterfly ( SFLY ) flitted nearly 9% higher after results showed it had trimmed losses more than expected for the first quarter. A 4% revenue gain topped targets. The stock is forming a cup with handle with a potential 84.81 buy point. Shutterfly has a weak 45 EPS rating from IBD, but earnings are expected to jump 145% this year, following a 133% EPS gain in 2017.
Snapchat parent Snap ( SNAP ) led the stocks moving lower on earnings news early Wednesday. The 14-month old stock dived 18% in premarket action. The Venice, Calif. outfit reported weaker-than-expected revenue growth, and an increase of 4 million daily active users during the quarter fell short of targets for a 7-million-user gain. Snapchat shares ended Tuesday down 33% from a February high, and 17% below the stock’s March 2017 IPO price .
